title: The SUPER Nova Study: A Randomised Pilot Study on Modulating Psychological Risk Factors in Chronic Pain
summary:
Chronic pain is one of the major causes of health impairments and reduced quality of life. Despite a wide range of treatment options, pain persists in many patients. In addition to physical causes, psychological factors often play an important role: adverse life events as well as pain-related anxiety and difficulties in managing distressing emotions can influence how the brain processes and maintains pain.
In the SUPER Nova study, we investigate the mechanisms of action of a brief intensive psychological intervention based on Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). EMDR is already successfully used for various mental health conditions and shows promising results for chronic pain. We want to understand why some chronic pain patients respond particularly well to this treatment while others respond less. To achieve this, we examine the psychological and biological factors that influence treatment success.
Study participants receive six EMDR sessions over two to three weeks and are randomly assigned to one of two treatment focuses. Using brain imaging, digital pain diaries, and specialised pain testing, we investigate the mechanisms through which EMDR exerts its effects. These insights should contribute to improving pain therapy in the long term and enable more targeted selection of the most suitable treatment for each individual patient.
conditions: Chronic Widespread Pain/ Fibromyalgia Syndrome (ICD-11: MG30.01)
Chronic primary musculoskeletal pain (focus on chronic primary low back pain) (ICD-11: MG30.02)
Chronic secondary musculoskeletal pain associated with structural changes (ICD-11: MG30.31)

interventions.name: Arm 1 (N = 61): Brief intensive intervention using Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) targeting memories related to adverse life events. The intervention comprises 6 sessions à 90 minutes over the course of 2-3 weeks.

Arm 2 (N = 61): Brief intensive intervention using Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) targeting pain-related anxiety and emotion dysregulation. The intervention comprises 6 sessions à 90 minutes over the course of 2-3 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients must meet the criteria for at least one of the following diagnoses: Chronic Widespread Pain/Fibromyalgia Syndrome (ICD-11: MG 30.01), Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CPRS, ICD-11: MG 30.04), Chronic Primary Low Back Pain (ICD-11: MG30.02), or Chronic Secondary Musculoskeletal Pain with Structural Changes (ICD-11: MG 30.31). At the time of inclusion, the chronic pain should have been present for at least three months. In addition, in order to be eligible for EMDR intervention, patients are required to have experienced at least one adverse life event with a relevant degree of current subjective distress and to exhibit a relevant level of pain catastrophising.
Exclusion criteria:
• Inflammatory conditions (e.g., rheumatic or systemic inflammatory diseases, acute pronounced inflammatory states)
• Diseases of the central nervous system (e.g., CNS resections, stroke, multiple sclerosis)
• Contraindications to EMDR therapy (e.g., acute psychosis or severe dissociation symptoms, pronounced personality disorders)
• Medication: antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, or opioids
• Ongoing psychotherapy at time of enrolment
